caveats: Material-based condition does not certify structural safety, building-code compliance or maintenance quality. Room counts are not bedroom counts or an overcrowding measure. Construction-period totals exclude container boxes and other units, giving 6,029,330 units rather than the 6,030,541 in the condition and room tables. Construction periods have unequal lengths and cannot be compared as annual building rates. The condition table combines urban and estate-urban; the room table separates them. Wall, roof and floor distributions are separate, overlapping views of the same units. Counts, shares and overlapping totals must not be added together; printed percentages, including 0.0, retain rounding.
Counts and one-decimal-place shares retain separate units. Construction-period coverage and residential-sector groupings differ by table.
grain: One housing condition, room, material or construction-period count/share by census geography in 2024
notes: The census classifies occupied housing as permanent, semi-permanent, improvised or not classified using wall, roof and floor materials. Counts and shares cover every district and the report’s sector groups. National tables also describe wall, roof and floor materials and construction periods. A separate sector table records one-room and multi-room housing.
